Amphilochius of Iconium was a Christian bishop of the fourth century, born around 339 or 340 into a distinguished Cappadocian family, perhaps at Caesarea. A cousin of Gregory of Nazianzus, he stood within the circle of the Cappadocian Fathers who shaped the Church's confession of the Trinity.

Chosen as bishop of Iconium in Lycaonia, he defended the orthodox faith against the Arian and Macedonian heresies. He took part in the Council of Constantinople in 381 and worked for the unity and orthodoxy of the Church. His writings earned him a place among the respected Fathers of that era.

He probably died between 394 and 403. He is venerated on November 22 in the Roman Catholic Church and on November 23 in the Orthodox Church, honored as a faithful bishop and defender of the faith.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Amphilochius grace to defend the truth of your Son's divinity, grant through his intercession that bishops and theologians may proclaim the faith with clarity and courage. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Amphilochius of Iconium

saints.name: St. Amun
saints.bio:
Amun, also called Ammon or Amoun, was a fourth-century Christian ascetic and founder of one of the most celebrated monastic communities in Egypt. Named after the ancient Egyptian god Amun, a reminder of the pagan world from which the early monks turned to Christ, he became one of the most venerated ascetics of the Nitrian Desert.

Athanasius of Alexandria mentions him in his Life of Anthony, and the great Antony is said to have regarded him as a fellow laborer. Amun gathered disciples and established a community that became a beacon of the new monastic movement, where men sought God through poverty, prayer, and obedience.

His feast is kept in the Coptic and Eastern traditions, and he is remembered as a pioneer of communal monastic life that shaped the Church for centuries.

prayer.text: O God, who stirred up St. Amun to gather a community of prayer in the desert, grant through his intercession that we may seek you with single-hearted devotion, above all worldly things. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Amun

saints.name: St. Amunia of San Millán
saints.bio:
Saint Amunia of San Millán was a Benedictine hermit of the La Rioja province in northern Spain, whose memory is inseparable from that of her daughter, Saint Áurea. After the death of her husband, Amunia turned from the world and followed Áurea into the hermit's life, mother and daughter making their way to the Monastery of San Millán de la Cogolla.

There in the valley of the Cárdenas river the two women gave themselves to prayer and contemplation within the shadow of the great Benedictine house that had shaped Spain's monastic awakening. Amunia's vocation was that of a widow who found in the cloister a second calling, and her example nourished the contemplative tradition of La Rioja.

Her feast is March 11.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Amunia from widowhood to the hermit's cell at San Millán, following her daughter St. Áurea into the life of contemplation, grant through her intercession that widows and all who mourn may find in You their lasting home. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anastasia of Sirmium
saints.bio:
Saint Anastasia is a Christian martyr who died at Sirmium in the Roman province of Pannonia Secunda, in what is now Serbia. She is honored in both East and West as one of the great early martyrs, and her cult spread quickly through the ancient Church, reaching Rome, where a basilica was dedicated to her.

In the Eastern Orthodox Church she is venerated as St. Anastasia the Pharmakolytria, a title meaning "Deliverer from Potions," also translated as "One who Cures Wounds." This points to her patronage of those who work with healing, especially of pharmacists, apothecaries, and physicians.

Her feast is kept on September 28 in the West and on December 25 in the East. She is remembered as a woman who faced death for her faith and is invoked by those who seek healing of body and soul.

prayer.text: O God, who made St. Anastasia a deliverer from every poison and a healer of wounds, grant through her intercession that the sick may find relief and those who care for them may serve with skill and love. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anastasia of Sirmium

saints.name: St. Anastasia the Patrician
saints.bio: Saint Anastasia the Patrician was a noble Byzantine courtier who served as lady-in-waiting to the Empress Theodora in Constantinople. When the emperor Justinian I reportedly turned his attentions toward her and Theodora grew jealous, Anastasia chose flight rather than scandal. She left the imperial city for Alexandria in Egypt and settled at Pempton, near the great metropolis, where she founded a monastery that would later bear her name. There she embraced monastic discipline with fervor, supporting herself by weaving cloth and living hidden in Christ. Her flight from worldly power became a passage into holiness, and her monastery became a house of prayer where she spent her days in penance and quiet devotion.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anastasia from the courts of emperors to the silence of the cloister, grant through her intercession that we may value purity of heart above earthly favor and find in hidden lives the peace that the world cannot give. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anastasia the Patrician

saints.name: St. Anastasius I of Antioch
saints.bio: Anastasius I of Antioch served twice as Patriarch of Antioch, one of the most ancient and prestigious sees of Christendom, during a period marked by theological controversy and political unrest. His first patriarchate was interrupted by deposition, yet he was later restored to his throne, governing the Church with patience and pastoral resolve through cycles of exile and return. Little biographical detail has survived beyond the fact of his dual tenure and the honor paid to his memory, but he is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church. His life recalls the fragility of ecclesiastical office in times of upheaval and the perseverance required of those entrusted with the care of divided sees.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Anastasius grace to govern your Church in times of trial and to return to his see after exile, grant through his intercession that all who suffer for the faith may remain steadfast and that your Church may be gathered again into one. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anastasius of Antioch
saints.bio:
Anastasius was a Christian convert who suffered martyrdom with Anthony, Julian, Celsus, and Marcionilla during the Diocletianic Persecution at the turn of the fourth century. He is said to have been raised from the dead by Saint Julian of Antioch and, upon that restoration, to have embraced the faith for which he would soon die.

His memorial is kept on January 9. Anastasius is one of the 140 Colonnade saints whose statues adorn St. Peter's Square in Rome, a testament to the memory of his witness. His relics were taken to the Ravanica Monastery in Serbia, where they are still honored.

He stands among the converts of the early Church whose new-found faith was proved by martyrdom. His story reminds the faithful that the grace of conversion can carry a soul even to the laying down of life.

prayer.text: O God, who raised up St. Anastasius to confess your name and to die for it, grant through his intercession that those who are newly come to faith may stand firm in trial. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anastasius of Antioch

saints.name: St. Anastasius Sinaita
saints.bio: Anastasius Sinaita, also called Anastasius of Sinai or Anastasius the Sinaite, was a Greek writer, priest, and abbot of Saint Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai. He defended the orthodox faith against the Monophysites, the Monothelites, and other theological movements that troubled the Church in the seventh century, composing treatises and homilies of enduring value. As abbot of one of the most ancient monasteries in Christendom, he cared for a community rooted at the foot of the mountain where Moses received the Law. He was widely read in the East for his scriptural exegesis and his collection of ascetic and moral teachings, the Hodegos or Guide, which instructed monks and priests in the discipline of the spiritual life.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Anastasius the Sinaite skill to defend the faith and to guide souls along the path of holiness, grant through his intercession that all who study your Word may be illumined by your Spirit and made worthy teachers of the Gospel. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anastasius Sinaita

saints.name: St. Anastasius the Fuller
saints.bio:
Saint Anastasius the Fuller was a Christian martyr of the pre-schism Church. A fuller by trade, one who worked in the cleaning and finishing of cloth, he plied this humble craft first at Aquileia before moving his business to Salona in Dalmatia, in what is now Croatia.

In Salona he lived as a working Christian at a time of imperial persecution. Arrested for his faith, Anastasius refused to renounce Christ and was put to death, joining the ranks of those whose ordinary labor became extraordinary through the witness of martyrdom.

He is remembered as a patron of those who work with their hands, and especially of fullers and dyers, trades now largely forgotten but once essential to daily life. His cult reminds the Church that holiness is found in every honest trade.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anastasius from the workshop to the crown of martyrdom, grant through his intercession that we may serve you faithfully in our daily work and bear witness to your name. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anathalon
saints.bio:
Saint Anathalon was the first recorded bishop of Milan, living at the end of the second or the beginning of the third century. He is honored as the founder of the church of Milan, one of the great sees of Italy, and a later tradition also named him the first bishop of Brescia.

He is venerated as a saint in both the Catholic and the Eastern Orthodox Churches. His feast is kept on September 24, though in Milan itself it is commemorated on September 25. He stands at the head of the long line of bishops who made Milan a center of Christian life and teaching.

prayer.text: O God, who established Your church at Milan through the first labors of Anathalon, grant through his intercession that the shepherds of Your people may build up the faith in every generation. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anathalon

saints.name: St. Andeolus
saints.bio:
Saint Andeolus, or Andeol, was a Christian missionary sent to preach the Gospel in Gaul, and is honored as a martyr of the early Church in southern France. According to tradition he was a disciple sent forth to bring the faith to the peoples of the Rhone valley, where he labored and finally gave his life.

His relics were long venerated at Bourg-Saint-Andeol, the town that bears his name. He is commemorated on May 1, and is remembered as one of the early heralds of the Gospel who planted the faith in Roman Gaul.

prayer.text: O God, who sent Andeolus to sow the seed of the Gospel in Gaul and crowned his labor with martyrdom, grant through his intercession that missionaries may proclaim Christ with courage unto the ends of the earth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Andeolus

saints.name: St. Andrew
saints.bio:
Andrew was a fisherman from Bethsaida in Galilee and the brother of Simon Peter. He was first a disciple of John the Baptist, who pointed him to Jesus as the Lamb of God. Andrew immediately followed Christ and then brought his brother Peter to him, becoming the first-called of the apostles.

According to tradition, Andrew preached the Gospel in Greece and Asia Minor and was martyred at Patras on an X-shaped cross, which came to be known as Saint Andrew's Cross. He is venerated as the patron saint of Scotland, Russia, and Greece.

As a fisherman by trade, Andrew is invoked as the patron saint of fishermen and all who work at sea.

prayer.text: O God, who called Andrew from his nets to follow Your Son and to bring his brother Peter to You, grant through his intercession that fishermen and all who labor at sea may be kept safe and draw many souls to Christ. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Andrew

saints.name: St. Andrew Kim Taegon
saints.bio:
Andrew Kim Taegon was born in 1821 into a Korean Catholic family during a time of fierce persecution. He was the first native Korean priest, ordained in Shanghai in 1845 after studying in Macau.

He returned to Korea to minister in secret, but was arrested in 1846 and beheaded near Seoul at the age of twenty-five. His father, Ignatius Kim, had been martyred years earlier.

He was canonized in 1984 by Pope John Paul II along with 102 other Korean martyrs, and is venerated as a patron of the Korean clergy.

prayer.text: O God, who strengthened Andrew Kim Taegon to return to Korea and minister in secret until he was beheaded at twenty-five, grant through his intercession that priests and all who suffer for the faith may remain faithful unto death. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Andrew Kim Taegon

saints.name: St. Andrew of Crete
saints.bio:
Andrew of Crete, also known as Andrew of Jerusalem, was an eighth-century bishop, theologian, homilist, and hymnographer whose literary and spiritual gifts enriched the Church of his age. Born in Damascus and raised in Jerusalem, he entered the monastic life and was eventually consecrated bishop of Gortyna on the island of Crete, where he served with distinction for many years.

Andrew is best remembered for his sermons and hymns, above all the Great Canon, a lengthy penitential hymn still sung in the Eastern churches during Lent. As a theologian he defended the faith and shepherded his flock with wisdom. Venerated as a saint in both the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Catholic Church, he stands as a bridge between the traditions of East and West and a model of eloquent, penitential preaching.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Andrew of Crete the gift of eloquence in preaching and the grace of penitential song, grant through his intercession that we may turn our hearts to you with sincere sorrow and proclaim your mercy in word and deed. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Andrew of Crete

saints.name: St. Andrew of Crete
saints.bio:
Andrew of Crete was a fervent iconophile who suffered martyrdom during the Byzantine Iconoclasm, executed in the Forum Bovis of Constantinople at the orders of Emperor Constantine V in 766 or 767. In an age when the veneration of sacred images was forbidden by imperial decree, Andrew boldly defended the holy icons as legitimate expressions of Christian faith, and he laid down his life rather than abandon this conviction.

He is regarded as a martyr in the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches. The monastery of St Andrew in Krisei in Constantinople, currently the Koca Mustafa Pasha Mosque in Istanbul, was dedicated to him. It should be noticed that according to modern sources, the figure of Andrew of Crete, like those of many iconophile saints who lived under the iconoclastic period, is unverified, yet his memory endures as a witness to the cost of fidelity to sacred tradition.

prayer.text: O God, who crowned St. Andrew of Crete with the palm of martyrdom for his fearless defense of your holy icons, grant through his intercession that we may venerate the sacred mysteries with faithful hearts and bear witness to your truth whatever the cost. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Andrew the Fool
saints.bio: Andrew of Constantinople is honored as a saint by the Eastern Orthodox Church and is revered as one of the famous fools for Christ, those holy men and women who took on the appearance of madness for the sake of the Gospel and so emptied themselves of worldly honor. Tradition holds that he wandered the streets of Constantinople bearing the mockery and contempt of the crowds while hidden from most eyes in divine wisdom, and that he was granted visions of the heavenly courts. By embracing folly for Christ's sake he followed the pattern of the Apostle who proclaimed the wisdom of the Cross as foolishness to the world. His feast is kept on 2 October. He is remembered as a fool-for-Christ, a mystic, and a living sign that the wisdom of God confounds the wisdom of this age.

prayer.text: O God, who made St. Andrew the Fool a living sign that the wisdom of the Cross is foolishness to the world, grant through his intercession that we may be freed from the love of human praise and may seek only the approval of Your eyes. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Andrew the Fool

saints.name: St. Andrew the Scot
saints.bio:
Andrew the Scot was an Irish-born cleric who crossed the sea to the continent in the early ninth century, one of that remarkable company of Irish monks and scholars who brought learning and faith to Carolingian Europe. He became the student and close assistant of Saint Donatus of Fiesole, accompanying the bishop to Tuscany and serving as archdeacon of Fiesole under his direction.

In that office he helped govern the diocese, foster the liturgy, and spread the gospel in the region around Fiesole, bringing to Italy the zeal for Scripture and monastic order that marked the Irish mission. His feast is kept on August 22, and he is honored as a patron of scholars, teachers, and of those who serve the Church far from the land of their birth.

prayer.text: O God, who led Saint Andrew the Scot from Ireland to serve your Church in Tuscany, granting him zeal for Scripture and devotion as archdeacon of Fiesole, grant through his intercession that scholars and teachers may bring light to every land they enter. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Andrew Zorard
saints.bio:
Saint Andrew Zorard was a Benedictine monk born in Poland who lived out his vocation in the kingdoms of Hungary, venerated in both the Catholic and Orthodox Churches. Drawn to the solitary life, he settled on a hill near Nitra in present-day Slovakia, where he built a hermitage and gave himself to prayer, fasting, and manual labor in the Slav wilderness.

His reputation drew disciples, and the monastic life he planted endured long after him, forming a bridge between the Latin and Byzantine traditions of the Carpathian basin. Nitra, the Dioceses of Nitra and Tarnów, and St. Andrew Abbey in Cleveland claim him as patron.

He died around 1040 and was buried on the hill of Zobor, where a cave and a spring associated with him were long venerated. His feast is June 13.

prayer.text: O God, who led St. Andrew Zorard from Poland to the hill of Zobor, there to plant the monastic life in the Carpathian wilderness, grant through his intercession that all who seek You in solitude may find You near. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Angela Merici
saints.bio:
Angela Merici was born around 1474 in Desenzano, Italy. Orphaned as a young woman, she joined the Third Order of St. Francis and devoted herself to the religious education of poor girls.

In 1535 she founded the Company of St. Ursula in Brescia, a community of women dedicated to teaching girls in their own homes. This became the foundation of the Ursuline Order, the first teaching order of women in the Church.

She died in 1540 and was canonized in 1807. She is venerated as the patron saint of teachers, educators, and the sick.

prayer.text: O God, who inspired Angela Merici to gather women to teach poor girls in their own homes, grant through her intercession that teachers may instruct the young with wisdom and love. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Angela Merici

saints.name: St. Angelar
saints.bio:
Saint Angelar was a medieval Bulgarian saint, venerated as one of the Seven Saints of Bulgaria whose work among the Slavic peoples earned them the title of enlighteners. He belonged to the circle of disciples formed in the wake of the mission of Saints Cyril and Methodius, carrying the gospel and the Slavonic liturgy into the lands beyond the Danube in the ninth century.

His labors helped lay the foundation of the Christian civilization of Bulgaria, translating prayer and Scripture into the tongue of the people and forming them in the faith. His feast is kept on July 27, and he is honored as a patron of missionaries, translators, and of all who labor to make the gospel intelligible in new cultures.

prayer.text: O God, who sent Saint Angelar among the Slavic peoples to proclaim your word in their own tongue, grant through his intercession that missionaries and translators may make the gospel known to every nation, and that all peoples may hear you speak in their own language. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Angelar

saints.name: St. Angelelmus
saints.bio:
Angelelmus was bishop of Auxerre from 813 to 828, one of the Carolingian-era pastors who governed the Church of Gaul through a time of reform and political upheaval. A Bavarian by birth, he came to Burgundy and served as abbot of the monastery of Saints Gervais and Protase at Auxerre before he was raised to the episcopal chair of the same city.

As bishop he cared for the clergy and people of his diocese through the years that followed the death of Charlemagne, when the empire was strained by division and invasion. His feast is kept on July 7, and he is honored as a patron of bishops and of monks, and as an intercessor for all who bear the weight of office in unsettled times.

prayer.text: O God, who called Saint Angelelmus from the abbey of Saints Gervais and Protase to the chair of Auxerre, granting him grace to govern in a time of trouble, grant through his intercession that all who hold office in your Church may serve with wisdom and courage. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anna the Prophetess
saints.bio:
Anna, a prophetess of the Tribe of Asher, is remembered in the Gospel of Luke as one of the first to bear witness to the infant Jesus. Widowed after seven years of marriage, she devoted her long life to prayer and fasting in the Temple, serving God night and day for some eighty-four years.

When Mary and Joseph brought Jesus for his presentation, Anna, filled with the Holy Spirit, gave thanks to God and spoke of the child to all who awaited the redemption of Jerusalem. Her encounter is recorded in Luke 2:36-38.

She is honored as a model of faithful widowhood and contemplation, counted among the earliest saints of the New Covenant, one whose eyes beheld the Lord's Christ.

prayer.text: O God, who called your handmaid Anna to a life of prayer and prophecy in your holy Temple, grant through her intercession that we may persevere in worship and recognize the presence of your Christ in our midst. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anna the Prophetess

saints.name: St. Anne
saints.bio:
Anne is honored as the mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary and the grandmother of Jesus. She is not mentioned in the Bible, but her story is told in the apocryphal Protoevangelium of James, which describes her and her husband Joachim as a devout couple who suffered many years of childlessness before God blessed them with a daughter, Mary.

Devotion to Anne developed early in the Eastern Church and spread throughout the West in the Middle Ages. She is especially venerated in France, where the shrine of Sainte-Anne-d'Auray and the basilica of Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré in Canada draw many pilgrims.

As the mother of Mary, Anne is a natural patron of mothers, grandmothers, and women hoping to conceive. She is also invoked by those who care for children and by homemakers.

prayer.text: O God, who after long years of waiting blessed Anne with the daughter who would bear the Savior, grant through her intercession that mothers and grandmothers may raise their children in faith and love. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anne

saints.name: St. Annemund
saints.bio: Saint Annemund, also known as Annemundus, Aunemundus, Ennemond, and Chamond, served as Archbishop of the Archdiocese of Lyon in the seventh century. He was a councillor of King Clovis II and a friend of the young Wilfrid of York, whom he encouraged and supported during the latter's early ecclesiastical career. He governed the Church of Lyon in the complex politics of Merovingian Gaul, when the great Frankish sees were drawn into the rivalry of courts and nobles. The year of his death is variously given as 657 or 658. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church, remembered as a pastor who held office at the intersection of throne and altar and who showed kindness to a future saint.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Annemund grace to serve your Church at Lyon and to encourage a younger laborer in the gospel, grant through his intercession that all pastors may guide with wisdom and that those who are called to your service may find faithful mentors. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Annemund

saints.name: St. Anno II
saints.bio:
Saint Anno II was Archbishop of Cologne from 1056 until his death and one of the great churchmen of the Salian age. From 1063 to 1065 he served as regent of the Holy Roman Empire for the minor Emperor Henry IV, bearing the weight of empire while shaping the reforming church of his day. He founded monasteries, among them Siegburg Abbey, a center of the Hirsau reform.

His career spanned the tensions of the Investiture Controversy: he counseled, corrected, and at times resisted the young Henry IV, navigating the cross-currents of Saxon and imperial politics. In Cologne he was remembered as a builder and patron, gathering relics and drawing scholars to the Rhineland.

He died on December 4, 1075, and was buried at Siegburg. Miracles at his tomb spread devotion, and he was later canonized.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Anno to Your Church as archbishop of Cologne and steersman of empire in a turbulent age, grant through his intercession that those who bear authority may serve Your peace and Your truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anno II

saints.name: St. Anselm, Duke of Friuli
saints.bio:
Anselm was the Lombard duke of Friuli from 749 to 751, a nobleman of high rank who nevertheless turned from worldly ambition to the service of God. After his tenure as duke, he laid aside the sword and founded the monastery of Nonantula, of which he became the first abbot, dedicating his later years to prayer, the governance of a religious community, and the cultivation of monastic life in northern Italy.

By his example Anselm showed that the goods of this world may be surrendered for the greater good of the kingdom of God. As a nobleman who became a monk, he is honored as a saint whose life bridged the worlds of secular authority and religious devotion. His foundation at Nonantula endured as a center of prayer and learning for centuries.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anselm from the honors of the world to the service of your house, grant through his intercession that we may esteem nothing above the love of your kingdom and order our lives in humble obedience to your will. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anselm, Duke of Friuli

saints.name: St. Anselm of Canterbury
saints.bio:
Anselm was born around 1033 in Aosta, in the Italian Alps. He left home as a young man and became a monk at the abbey of Bec in Normandy, where he taught and wrote, and where he composed his famous works on the existence of God, including the Proslogion with its ontological argument.

In 1093 he became Archbishop of Canterbury, where he defended the rights of the Church against the English kings and was twice exiled. His writings on the atonement, Cur Deus Homo, shaped Western theology for centuries.

He died in 1109 and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1720. He is venerated as a patron of philosophers and theologians.

prayer.text: O God, who taught Anselm that faith seeks understanding and gave him courage to defend Your Church in exile, grant through his intercession that philosophers and theologians may let faith enlighten their reason and their reason serve the truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anselm of Canterbury

saints.name: St. Anselm of Lucca
saints.bio:
Saint Anselm of Lucca, born Anselm of Baggio, was a medieval bishop of Lucca and a prominent figure in the Investiture Controversy that rent the eleventh-century Church. His uncle, also named Anselm, had preceded him as bishop of Lucca before being raised to the papacy as Alexander II, and so he is sometimes called Anselm the Younger or Anselm II.

Caught up in the struggle between the Countess Matilda of Tuscany and the Emperor Henry IV, Anselm stood with the reforming party of Gregory VII, refusing investiture from lay hands and suffering exile for the liberty of the Church. He guided the see of Lucca through years of faction and strife with a confessor's courage.

He died on March 18, 1086, and was honored as a saint in Lucca and beyond. Mantua also venerates him as patron.

prayer.text: O God, who strengthened St. Anselm of Lucca to defend the freedom of Your Church in the storm of the Investiture Controversy, grant through his intercession that bishops may never yield the truth to the powers of this world. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anselm of Lucca

saints.name: St. Ansfried of Utrecht
saints.bio:
Saint Ansfried of Utrecht, sometimes called Ansfried the Younger, was Count of Huy and sword-bearer to the Emperor Otto I before he laid down sword and title to become Bishop of Utrecht in 995. He was the son or grandson of Lambert, a nobleman of the Maasgau, the very district where he later founded the Abbey of Thorn, the first women's religious house in the Low Countries.

At Otto's court he had been a warrior and a counsellor; as bishop he turned to the care of souls, the building of churches, and the relief of the poor, embodying the Ottonian ideal of the nobleman turned pastor. He spent himself in the humble service of his diocese.

Blind in his final years, Ansfried resigned his see and withdrew to a monastery, where he died around 1010. He was honored as a saint at Utrecht and Huy.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Ansfried from the sword-bearer's post to the shepherd's staff, making him bishop of Utrecht and father of the Abbey of Thorn, grant through his intercession that all who bear arms may learn the ways of peace. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Ansfried of Utrecht

saints.name: St. Ansgar
saints.bio:
Ansgar, the "Apostle of the North," was born in northern France in 801 and entered the Benedictine monastery of Corbie as a boy. Ordained young, he felt a call to bring the gospel to the pagan peoples of the north, and in 826 he traveled to Denmark as a missionary with the backing of the emperor, then pressed on to Sweden, preaching and gathering a small flock at the cost of great hardship.

As Archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen he received the missionary mandate for all of Scandinavia, and for the rest of his life he labored to plant the Church among the Danes, Swedes, and peoples of the Baltic, returning again and again though his converts were few and his churches often destroyed. He died in 865, a patron of missionaries and a model of perseverance in the face of meager results.

prayer.text: O God, who sent Saint Ansgar as the Apostle of the North to proclaim the gospel to the peoples of Scandinavia, granting him perseverance though his harvest was small, grant through his intercession that missionaries may never grow weary in sowing your word. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Ansgar

saints.name: St. Ansovinus
saints.bio:
Saint Ansovinus was a bishop of Camerino in the Marches of Italy in the ninth century, venerated from ancient times as a patron of agriculture and of all who work the land. The traditions of his diocese remember him as a pastor who cared for the bodies as well as the souls of his people, blessing the fields and praying for the harvest in a region where the rhythms of sowing and reaping shaped every life.

His intercession was sought especially for good weather and fruitful harvests, and gardeners and farmers looked to him in the seasons of planting and reaping. His feast is kept on March 13, and he is honored as a patron of gardeners, farmers, and of all who ask God's blessing on the work of their hands.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Saint Ansovinus a pastor's care for both the souls and the fields of Camerino, granting him love for those who labor in the earth, bless through his intercession the work of gardeners and farmers, and give us our daily bread in due season. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Ansovinus

saints.name: St. Ansurius
saints.bio: Ansurius was a Galician bishop who shepherded the diocese of Orense in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, becoming its bishop in 915. After years of governing his see, he gave up his post in 922 to embrace the monastic life at the monastery of Ribas de Sil, which he himself had helped to found. In laying down the cares of the episcopate for the silence of the cloister, he followed the ancient ideal of a bishop who ends his days as a monk. He is venerated as a saint in both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches, and his feast is kept on 26 January. He is remembered as a pastor who chose the monastery over the palace and who rounded out his episcopal labors with the pursuit of contemplation.

prayer.text: O God, who led St. Ansurius from the chair of a bishop to the silence of a monastery, grant through his intercession that pastors may long for the contemplation of Your face and that monks may show forth the peace of the world to come. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anthelm of Belley
saints.bio: Anthelm of Belley, born in 1107 into a noble family of the Château district of Faucigny in Savoy, was destined from youth for an ecclesiastical career. As a young priest he held a lucrative provostship and lived comfortably until a conversation with his uncle, a Carthusian prior, stirred him to seek a life of penance. He entered the Grande Chartreuse, motherhouse of the Carthusian Order, and so distinguished himself by wisdom and discipline that within a few years he was elected prior of the whole Order. He restored the spiritual fervor of the houses and governed with firmness and charity. Later called to become Bishop of Belley, he devoted himself to reforming clergy and flock. He died June 26, 1178. He is remembered as a monk-bishop who brought cloister discipline to Church governance.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anthelm from the ease of the world to the discipline of the hermitage and then to the pastoral care of a diocese, grant through his intercession that those who govern Your Church may serve with humility and zeal. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthelm of Belley

saints.name: St. Anthony Mary Claret
saints.bio:
Anthony Mary Claret was born in Sallent, Spain, in 1807. After working as a weaver, he was ordained a priest in 1835 and spent a decade preaching popular missions across Catalonia and the Canary Islands, drawing enormous crowds with his direct, fiery style.

In 1849 he founded the Congregation of Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, known as the Claretians, and established a religious publishing house that printed millions of books and pamphlets. In 1850 he was named Archbishop of Santiago, Cuba, where he reformed the seminary and defended the enslaved.

Recalled to Spain as confessor to Queen Isabella II, he died in exile in France in 1870 and was canonized in 1950. He is venerated as a patron of publishers, the Catholic press, and weavers.

prayer.text: O God, who made Anthony Mary Claret a weaver, then a missionary who printed millions of books and defended the enslaved in Cuba, grant through his intercession that publishers and weavers may spread the Gospel and clothe the world in charity. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony Mary Claret

saints.name: St. Anthony of Kiev
saints.bio:
Saint Anthony of Kiev, also called Anthony of the Caves, was the founder of the monastic tradition in Kievan Rus'. Born in the eleventh century, he journeyed as a young man to Mount Athos and embraced the ascetic life among hermits living in caves. He was tonsured with the name Anthony in memory of the desert father.

Returning to Kiev, he settled in a cave on the bluff above the Dnieper and gave himself to prayer, fasting, and silence. Disciples gathered, and with Saint Theodosius he co-founded the Kiev Pechersk Lavra, the Monastery of the Caves, which became the spiritual heart of Russian and Ukrainian Orthodoxy.

Anthony later withdrew again to the solitude of the caves, leaving Theodosius to guide the community. He died in the late eleventh century, and his relics rest in the Lavra.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anthony of Kiev from Mount Athos to the caves above the Dnieper, there to plant the monastic life in the land of Rus', grant through his intercession that we may seek You in stillness and persevering prayer. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony of Kiev

saints.name: St. Anthony of Padua
saints.bio:
Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões in Lisbon, Portugal, around 1195, Anthony joined the Augustinian canons as a young man. Inspired by the martyrdom of Franciscan missionaries in Morocco, he transferred to the Franciscan Order and took the name Anthony, hoping to preach to Muslims. Illness forced him to return to Europe, where his ship was driven to Sicily, and he settled in Italy.

Anthony's extraordinary preaching and knowledge of Scripture were discovered almost by accident when he was asked to speak at an ordination. He became one of the most celebrated preachers of his age, drawing vast crowds across Italy and France, and was known for miracles, including the famous sermon to the fishes. He taught theology with the blessing of St. Francis himself.

He died at Arcella near Padua on June 13, 1231, at about age 36, and was canonized less than a year later in 1232. Today he is one of the most beloved saints in the world, invoked especially for the recovery of lost items and as a patron of travelers.

prayer.text: O Holy St. Anthony, gentlest of saints, your love for God and charity for his creatures made you worthy, when on earth, to possess miraculous powers. Encouraged by this thought, I implore you to obtain for me my request. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony of Padua

saints.name: St. Anthony of Rome
saints.bio: Anthony of Rome, also called Anthony the Roman, was a twelfth-century monk who founded the Antoniev Monastery in Novgorod, Russia. Born in Rome, he entered a monastery there, but when the Latin Church turned to customs his conscience could not accept, he fled. A storm at sea carried him miraculously, in a single day, from Rome to the shores of the Great Novgorod, a journey that should have taken weeks. Settling as a hermit near the city, he gathered disciples. He founded the monastery dedicated to the Nativity of the Theotokos, and the house bore his name, Antoniev. He governed his monks with gentleness and was revered for his holiness. He died around 1147. His feast is kept on January 17. He is remembered as a wanderer for the truth who found his home where God's providence brought him.

prayer.text: O God, who by a marvelous providence brought St. Anthony of Rome across the sea to a new home and a new work for Your Church, grant through his intercession that those who wander in search of truth may find their rest in You. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony of Rome

saints.name: St. Anthony the Abbot
saints.bio:
Anthony was born around 251 in Egypt to wealthy Christian parents. After hearing the Gospel command to sell everything and give to the poor, he gave away his inheritance and withdrew to the desert to live a life of prayer and asceticism.

He spent decades in solitude, and his holiness drew disciples who gathered around him, making him the father of Christian monasticism. St. Athanasius wrote his biography, which spread his example throughout the Christian world. Anthony lived to the age of about 105, dying in 356.

In the Middle Ages, an order of hospitallers known as the Antonines cared for the sick, and their pigs were allowed to roam freely, which is why Anthony is often pictured with a pig. He is venerated as the patron saint of butchers, gravediggers, and those who work with animals.

prayer.text: O God, who moved Anthony to sell all he had and follow Your Son into the desert, grant through his intercession that butchers and all who seek You in solitude may resist temptation and grow in holiness. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony the Abbot

saints.name: St. Anthony the Confessor
saints.bio:
Anthony the Confessor served as Archbishop of Thessalonica from 843 until his death, governing the great Byzantine see during the years that followed the final restoration of the veneration of icons. Most of what is known of his life comes through the vita of his relative Saint Theodora of Thessalonica, with whom he is linked in the memory of the Eastern Church.

As archbishop he shepherded the Church of Thessalonica through the aftermath of the iconoclast controversy, defending the faith of the icons and guiding his people back into the fullness of Catholic worship. He is venerated like Theodora on November 2, and is honored as a patron of bishops, confessors, and of all who defend the Church's ancient traditions in times of dispute.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Saint Anthony the Confessor grace to govern the Church of Thessalonica and defend the veneration of your holy icons, grant through his intercession that we may hold fast to the faith of the ages and be united in your truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anthony the Great
saints.bio:
Saint Anthony the Great, called the Father of All Monks, was an Egyptian Christian who lived in the third and fourth centuries and is revered as the founder of Christian monasticism. Born around 251 of prosperous peasant parents, he gave away his inheritance after hearing the Gospel call to sell all and follow Christ, and withdrew into the desert to live in solitude and prayer.

He endured long years of ascetic struggle and spiritual combat, and his example drew disciples who formed the first communities of monks. He supported the Church during the Arian controversy, boldly confessing the divinity of Christ. He died around 356, and is invoked as a patron of animals, farmers, hermits, and monks, and of the poor whom he loved.

prayer.text: O God, who called Anthony into the desert to combat the powers of evil and to seek You in solitude, grant through his intercession that we may overcome the temptations of this world and love You above all. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony the Great

saints.name: St. Anthony the Hermit
saints.bio:
Anthony the Hermit, also known as Anthony of Lérins, was an anchorite of the early Church. Born in the Roman province of Pannonia Valeria, then part of the Hunnic Empire, he was drawn to the solitary life of prayer and journeyed westward, settling among the monastic community at Lérins, off the southern coast of Gaul.

At Lérins, where Vincent of Lérins and other holy men had set the pattern of contemplative life, Anthony gave himself to silence, fasting, and the struggle of the desert transplanted to an island. He is counted among those hermits who carried the ideals of the Egyptian desert into the West.

Venerated in both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches, his feast is December 28, and he is remembered as one who brought the quiet flame of the desert to a new land.

prayer.text: O God, who called Anthony from the land of his birth to the solitude of Lérins, grant through his intercession that we may seek You in quietness of heart and find in prayer the strength to serve. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anthony the Hermit

saints.name: St. Anthusa of Mantinea
saints.bio:
Saint Anthusa of Mantinea, also called Anthusa the Confessor, was an anchoress and abbess in Constantinople during the eighth century. Choosing the path of severe asceticism, she withdrew from the world to a life of solitude and unceasing prayer, and later became the head of a community of women religious in the imperial city.

As a confessor of the faith, Anthusa endured the trials of her age with steadfastness, bearing witness to the Gospel through the silent eloquence of her life. Her witness as both anchoress and abbess made her a model of the contemplative and communal dimensions of the consecrated life, and she has been venerated from ancient times as a holy woman who sought God with all her heart.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Anthusa to seek you in solitude and to guide others in the way of holiness, grant through her intercession that we may find in prayer the wellspring of our strength and lead others to you by the example of our lives. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Antonina and Alexander
saints.bio:
Saints Antonina and Alexander, venerated also as Theodora and Didymus, are Christian martyrs whose legend rests on a fourth-century acta and the witness of Saint Ambrose. According to the ancient account, the noblewoman, wishing to preserve her virginity, fled and disguised herself as a man in a monastery. When her sex was discovered and she was condemned, the soldier who uncovered her repented, declared himself a Christian, and died beside her.

They were martyred under Diocletian and Maximianus. Their feast is April 5, and their mutual witness has been told across the centuries as a sign of courage and conversion.

This Theodora is not to be confused with another of Alexandria commemorated on September 11. They stand among the martyrs whose self-giving made them companions in glory.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Antonina and St. Alexander grace to die together for the name of Christ, grant through their intercession that we may be steadfast in chastity and brave in confession of your name. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Antonina and Alexander

saints.name: St. Antoninus of Sorrento
saints.bio:
Antoninus of Sorrento was an Italian abbot and hermit of the early medieval Church, one of those southern Italian monks whose holiness was formed in solitude and bore fruit in the care of others. Born in the region of Campagna, he was drawn from his youth to the life of prayer and withdrew to live as a hermit before he was called to govern a community as abbot.

As abbot he gathered disciples around the monastic rule and led them in the pursuit of God, while his reputation for holiness spread through the countryside around Sorrento. His feast is kept on February 14, and he is honored as a patron of hermits, monks, and contemplatives, and as an intercessor for all who seek God in silence.

prayer.text: O God, who called Saint Antoninus from solitude to guide a community of monks in the hills above Sorrento, granting him wisdom in both silence and service, grant through his intercession that we may seek you in quiet and find you in the company of our brothers and sisters. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Antoninus of Sorrento

saints.name: St. Antony the Younger
saints.bio: Saint Antony the Younger served as a Byzantine military officer before renouncing the world to embrace the monastic life. After years in imperial service, he withdrew to a monastery, trading the sword for the cowl and dedicating himself to prayer, fasting, and the ascetic disciplines of the Eastern Church. His conversion from the camps and campaigns of the empire to the silence of the cloister made him a living sign that even the soldier may become a contemplative. Venerated by the Eastern Orthodox Church, he is commemorated on 1 December as a monk who put off the armor of war to take up the armor of Christ.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Antony the Younger from the ranks of soldiers to the silence of the monastery, grant through his intercession that all who serve in arms may find the way to peace, and that all monks may persevere in prayer. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Anysia of Thessalonica
saints.bio:
Saint Anysia of Thessalonica was a Christian virgin and martyr of the fourth century. Born to pious and affluent parents who raised her in Christian piety, she was left their wealth when they died while she was still young. She freely distributed it to the poor, choosing for herself a strict life of fasting, vigil, and prayer.

Her martyrdom is set in the reign of the emperor Maximinus, who renewed persecution against the Christians. According to tradition, a soldier met her as she left a place of prayer and, when she refused the pagan sacrifice, struck and killed her. Her relics were honored at the Basilica of Saint Demetrios.

Her feast is kept on December 30. She is remembered as a virgin who gave her wealth to the poor and her life to Christ, and invoked as a patron of single women.

prayer.text: O God, who made St. Anysia a virgin rich in poverty and brave in martyrdom, grant through her intercession that we may hold lightly to the goods of this world and firmly to the gift of our faith. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Anysia of Thessalonica

saints.name: St. Aphrahat
saints.bio:
Aphrahat, venerated as the Persian Sage, was a third-century Syriac Christian author from the Sasanian Empire, a region then beyond the eastern boundaries of Roman rule. Of Iranian descent, he composed twenty-three expositions on Christian doctrine and practice known as the Demonstrations, among the earliest surviving works of Syriac theology.

An ascetic and celibate, Aphrahat was almost certainly a son of the covenant, one set apart for prayer and the study of Scripture. Later Syriac tradition places him at the head of Mar Mattai Monastery near Mosul in what is now northern Iraq, and he may have been a bishop. He was a near contemporary of Ephrem the Syrian, though Ephrem lived within the Roman sphere.

His writings witness to the concerns of the early Church outside the Empire, addressing faith, prayer, asceticism, and the life of God's people under Persian rule. Honored as a pioneer of Syriac Christian thought, his feast is kept on January 29.

prayer.text: O God, who enlightened St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage to set forth the truths of faith in the Syriac tongue for a Church far from the centers of worldly power, grant through his intercession that we may love Your truth and bear witness to it in simplicity of life. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Aphrahat

saints.name: St. Apollinaris Claudius
saints.bio:
Saint Apollinaris Claudius—also called Apollinaris of Hierapolis or Apollinaris the Apologist—was a Christian leader and writer of the second century, one of the first to raise his voice in defense of the faith against the calumnies that surrounded the young Church. As bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia, he stands among the noble company of early apologists who sought to explain the Gospel to the Greco-Roman world and refute the Gnostic errors that pressed in on every side.

Eusebius of Caesarea preserves fragments of his writings, commending his learning and zeal for the truth. His feast is kept on January 8, and he is invoked as a patron of writers and theologians, that they may defend the faith with clarity, courage, and charity.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Saint Apollinaris Claudius the wisdom to defend your Gospel and the courage to raise his voice for the truth in the Church's first centuries, grant through his prayers that writers and theologians may proclaim your word with clarity and love. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Apollinaris Claudius

saints.name: St. Apollinaris of Valence
saints.bio: Saint Apollinaris of Valence was born in Vienne, Gaul, around 453 and became bishop of Valence in the turbulent decades of the barbarian irruptions. The see he inherited had lain vacant for fifty years after the scandalous reign of the dissolute Bishop Maximus, and the Church in that region needed a shepherd of firm faith and clean heart. Apollinaris undertook the restoration of his diocese amid the upheavals of the early Burgundian kingdom, ruling his flock with diligence through years of political disorder and moral collapse. He served as bishop until his death around 520, leaving the see renewed and the faithful strengthened. He was buried in what is now Valence Cathedral, which honors his memory to this day.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Apollinaris the grace to restore a see long desolate and to shepherd your people through times of turmoil, grant through his intercession that all bishops may be steadfast in faith and pure in life. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Apollinaris of Valence

saints.name: St. Apollinaris Syncletica
saints.bio:
Apollinaris Syncletica, also known as Apollinaria of Egypt, was a saint and hermit of the fifth century, venerated in both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. Her story, most likely apocryphal, turns on the theme of a devout girl who put on male attire and lived for many years undiscovered among the monks of the desert, seeking God free from a woman's obligations.

According to the legend, she withdrew to the desert of Scetis disguised as a man named Dorotheus, and lived as a hermit of such austerity that her own father, sent to seek her counsel, did not recognize her. Only at her death was her sex revealed, and the monks who had revered her were astonished.

The Church honors her as a model of the desire for God that overrides every constraint. Her feast is January 4.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Apollinaris Syncletica a longing for the desert that overcame every fear, grant through her intercession that those who seek You in solitude may be sustained by Your grace. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Apollonia
saints.bio:
Apollonia was a deaconess of the church of Alexandria who was martyred around 249, during a riot against Christians that followed the edict of the emperor Decius. An elderly woman of great virtue, she was seized by a mob that beat her and knocked out or broke all of her teeth.

Her captors built a fire and threatened to throw her into it unless she renounced Christ. Asking for a moment to pray, she then leapt into the flames herself rather than deny her faith.

Because of the torture she endured, Apollonia is invoked against toothache and all diseases of the teeth. She is the patron saint of dentistry and of dentists, and is often depicted holding a tooth in a pair of pincers.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Apollonia courage to leap into the flames rather than deny Your Son, grant through her intercession relief to all who suffer toothache and skill to those who care for their teeth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Apollonia

saints.name: St. Apollonius and Philemon
saints.bio:
Apollonius, a deacon, and his convert Philemon were Christian martyrs of the Diocletianic Persecution, put to death around 303 at Antinoöpolis in Egypt. Philemon had been a famous flute player, mime, and actor in the city, well known for his public performances.

According to tradition, Apollonius was arrested for his faith, and Philemon, moved by the deacon's witness, professed himself a Christian and was arrested alongside him. Both refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods and were condemned to death, winning the martyr's crown together.

Honored on March 8, they are remembered as patrons of dancers and performers, the arts by which Philemon once made his living now consecrated by his witness to Christ.

prayer.text: O God, who by the shedding of blood united the deacon Apollonius and the performer Philemon in one confession of faith, grant through their intercession that all who serve in the arts may find in You the source of their gifts and the courage to bear witness to Your truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Apollonius and Philemon

saints.name: St. Apronia of Toul
saints.bio: Saint Apronia of Toul, also called Evronie of Troyes, was a nun and saint of the sixth century. Born at Tranquille, a village near Trier in Germany, she was the sister of Saint Aprus of Toul, a bishop in northeastern France, from whose hand she received the religious veil. Drawn by love of Christ to the monastic life, she led, in the words of the hagiographer Sabine Baring-Gould, a virginal and angelic life, loving innocence, purity, and holiness to her dying day. She died in a convent at Troyes on the fifteenth of July and was solemnly enshrined at Toul by Bishop Saint Gerard in the year 992. She is invoked as the patroness of women in labor and of those who face danger in childbirth.

prayer.text: O God, who preserved St. Apronia in innocence and purity through all her days, look with mercy upon mothers in labor and all who face danger in childbirth, and through her intercession grant them safe deliverance and the joy of new life. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Apronia of Toul

saints.name: St. Aprunculus of Trier
saints.bio: Saint Aprunculus of Trier became Bishop of Trier around the year 525, succeeding Fibicius in one of the most ancient and illustrious sees of Gaul. Though his episcopate was brief, serving only about a year before his own death in 526, he inherited a diocese shaped by centuries of Christian witness in the Rhineland. Trier had been a stronghold of the faith since Roman times, and Aprunculus governed it in a period of transition between the late antique and early medieval worlds. He was succeeded by Nicetius, another noted bishop of Trier. Though the records of his life are sparse, his inclusion in the roll of the saints of Trier testifies to a reputation for holiness recognized by the faithful of his time.

prayer.text: O God, who in every age raises up shepherds for your Church, grant through the intercession of St. Aprunculus that those who govern dioceses may serve with fidelity, however brief their tenure, and leave behind a legacy of faithfulness. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Aprunculus of Trier

saints.name: St. Aquilinus of Milan
saints.bio:
Saint Aquilinus of Milan, also known as Aquilinus of Cologne, is venerated as a martyr by the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Churches. Born into a noble family, he studied in Cologne and was ordained a missionary priest. Fired with zeal for souls, he traveled as a preacher through Germany and other European lands, declaring the Gospel where the old paganisms still lingered.

Tradition holds that after years of missionary labor Aquilinus returned to the region of Milan, where he confronted heresy and was slain by enemies of the faith, winning the martyr's crown. His relics were honored at Milan, where he became a patron of the city's working people.

He is invoked especially by the hotel porters, the facchini of Milan. He was canonized before the formal process of canonization existed.

prayer.text: O God, who crowned the missionary labors of St. Aquilinus with the palm of martyrdom, grant through his intercession that we may bear witness to Your truth with courage, and that all who serve travelers and strangers may find in You their reward. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Aquilinus of Milan

saints.name: St. Arbeo of Freising
saints.bio:
Saint Arbeo of Freising was an early medieval author and the Bishop of Freising from 764, a see he governed during the formative decades of the Bavarian church. As a bishop he oversaw the consolidation of Christian life in his diocese and promoted the establishment of churches and monasteries, while as an author he composed works that recorded the deeds of the early saints of his region, notably the Life of St. Corbinian.

Arbeo was among the first writers of the Bavarian church, and his literary efforts helped to preserve the memory of the holy men and women who brought the Gospel to southern Germany. He served his see with care and died in office, honored by his clergy and people. He is remembered as a learned bishop and a faithful shepherd of an emerging Christian community.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Arbeo the gifts of learning and pastoral care and made him a faithful shepherd of your people in Freising, grant through his intercession that those who lead your Church may also preserve the memory of your saints and teach the faithful with wisdom. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arbeo of Freising

saints.name: St. Archelais and Companions
saints.bio:
Saints Archelais, Thecla, and Susanna were Christian virgins of the Romagna region of northern Italy. During the persecution under Diocletian in the third century, they disguised themselves as men, cut their hair, and fled to a remote part of Campagna in southern Italy.

There they lived as ascetics, devoted to fasting and prayer, and God granted them a gift of healing by which they treated the local inhabitants and converted many pagans. When the governor heard of their works, he arrested them and brought them to Salerno. He threatened Archelais with torture if she would not sacrifice to the idols; she refused, and the lions set upon her meekly lay at her feet. Imprisoned and condemned, they are honored as martyrs.

prayer.text: O God, who gave the virgins Archelais, Thecla, and Susanna grace to heal bodies and souls and courage to face the lions for Your name, grant through their intercession that all who suffer may find healing and hope in You. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Archil of Kakheti
saints.bio:
Prince Archil the Martyr was an eighth-century Georgian Orthodox Christian royal prince of the eastern Georgian region of Kakheti. As a member of the ruling house, he governed his people during a period of intense pressure from the neighboring Islamic powers, and he refused to renounce the Christian faith despite the threats and violence brought against him. For his steadfastness he was put to death, and he has been venerated ever since as a martyr of the Georgian church.

Archil's sacrifice stands as a witness to the long and costly fidelity of the Georgian people to the Gospel of Christ. As a royal prince who chose death rather than apostasy, he is honored among the martyrs of the Caucasus and remembered as a patron of those who suffer for the name of Christ in that ancient Christian land.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Archil of Kakheti the courage to lay down his life rather than deny the name of your Son, grant through his intercession that we may confess our faith with boldness and stand firm against every force that would turn us from you. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Arethas of Najran
saints.bio: Saint Arethas, known in Arabic as Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb, was the leader of the Miaphysite Christian community of Najran in the early sixth century. In the year 523 he was executed during the persecution of Christians by Dhu Nuwas, the king of Yemen, who sought to force the faithful to renounce Christ. Arethas and his companions refused, and their martyrdom became one of the most stirring episodes in the ancient chronicles of Christian persecution. News of their sacrifice spread swiftly, reaching Emperor Justin I of Byzantium and the Christian Kingdom of Aksum in Ethiopia, who sent armies to depose Dhu Nuwas and end the persecution. Arethas stands as a witness to courage in faith, a leader who chose death rather than betrayal of the Gospel.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Arethas and his companions the grace to face death rather than deny your Son, grant through their intercession that all who suffer for the faith may stand firm, and that persecutors everywhere may be turned toward the light of Christ. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arethas of Najran

saints.name: St. Ariadne of Phrygia
saints.bio:
Saint Ariadne of Phrygia is honored as a Christian martyr of the second century, one of the confessors who shed their blood for Christ in the Roman province of Phrygia, in Asia Minor, where the Gospel had taken root early and deep. The ancient traditions of the Greek and Syriac churches remember her as a slave who refused to renounce her faith and who, by the grace of God, won the crown of martyrdom rather than deny her Lord.

In an age when confessing Christ could cost everything, Ariadne chose the better part, joining the virgin martyrs venerated from the Church's earliest days. She is invoked as a patron of martyrs and of slaves—of all who are bound and oppressed, that they may know the freedom that only Christ can give, and the dignity no earthly master can take away.

prayer.text: O God, who gave Saint Ariadne of Phrygia the grace to prefer death to the denial of your Son, grant through her intercession that all who are bound and oppressed may know the freedom of your children and that we may bear witness to your name with constancy. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Ariadne of Phrygia

saints.name: St. Arialdo
saints.bio:
Saint Arialdo was a Christian saint of the eleventh century, a nobleman of Milan and a canon of the cathedral chapter, who gave his life to reform the clergy of his city. When simony and clerical concubinage had spread through the Lombard church, Arialdo joined the Pataria, the lay reform movement led by his kinsman St. Heribert, preaching repentance to priests and people alike.

His zeal made him enemies among the clergy whose abuses he exposed. He was repeatedly threatened, assaulted, and excommunicated by a hostile faction, yet pressed on with the support of Pope Alexander II. In 1066 he was ambushed by armed men near Milan, murdered, and his body thrown into Lake Maggiore.

The people of Milan reverenced him as a martyr, and his relics were later enshrined in the Cathedral of Milan.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Arialdo the courage to plead for holiness among the clergy of Milan even to the shedding of his blood, grant through his intercession that Your people may never grow weary of seeking reform and justice in Your Church. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arialdo

saints.name: St. Arilda of Oldbury
saints.bio:
Saint Arilda, also called Saint Arild, was a female saint of Oldbury-on-Severn in the English county of Gloucestershire. She probably lived in the fifth or sixth century, in that twilight generation when Roman Britain had faded and the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms were still young, and she may have been of either Anglo-Saxon or Welsh origin.

Almost nothing certain survives about her life. Her memory is bound to the place where she was venerated, at Oldbury-on-Severn and at the nearby Oldbury-on-the-Hill, both in Gloucestershire, where her name was kept in the local calendars and her feast observed by the villagers.

Her feast is July 20. The Church honors her as one of the hidden saints of England, whose devotion took root in the soil of a particular place and endured.

prayer.text: O God, who kept the memory of St. Arilda alive among the people of Oldbury through the centuries, grant through her intercession that the faithful of England may hold fast to the holiness planted in their land. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arilda of Oldbury

saints.name: St. Aristides of Athens
saints.bio:
Aristides of Athens was a 2nd-century Christian philosopher and one of the earliest apologists of the Church. Born into a cultured Athenian family, he embraced the faith in its first generations and set about defending it before the learned world of his day.

His surviving work, the Apology of Aristides, is among the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament. Addressed to the Emperor Hadrian, it argues that Christians alone live the truth they profess, comparing their morals with those of Greeks, barbarians, and Jews. The text was lost to the West for centuries before a Syriac manuscript was recovered in the 19th century.

Aristides is honored as a model of reasoned defense of the faith, a witness that the gospel has always had thoughtful advocates among the philosophers.

prayer.text: O God, who gave St. Aristides the wisdom to defend the faith before the rulers of this world, grant through his intercession that we may give an account of the hope that is in us with gentleness and truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Aristides of Athens

saints.name: St. Armel
saints.bio: Saint Armel was an early sixth-century holy man of Brittany, one of the many Celtic and Breton saints whose lives are known to us more through local devotion than through detailed written record. He belongs to the great age of Breton sanctity, when monks and hermits carried the faith across the western edges of Christendom, establishing hermitages, preaching the Gospel, and shaping the religious landscape of Armorica. Though the surviving particulars of his life are few, his memory endured in the piety of the Breton people, who honored him as one of their own. His feast is kept on August 16. He is invoked as a patron of Brittany and remembered among the holy men who brought Christ to the far shores of the Celtic world.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Armel to the wild and windswept shores of Brittany, there to live for you in solitude and prayer, grant through his intercession that we may find in stillness the presence we too often seek in noise. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Armel

saints.name: St. Arn
saints.bio: Saint Arn, called Arno von Endsee, was elected Bishop of Würzburg in 855 upon the death of his master Bishop Gozbald. A warrior-prelate in an age of ceaseless frontier warfare, Arn was recorded fighting against nearly every external foe that pressed upon the German peoples during his episcopate. He governed the see until his death, defending both the church and the realm with pastoral care and with the sword. His life testifies to the turbulent ninth century, when bishops were shepherds and war-leaders at once, charged with the survival of Christian peoples under constant threat from invaders on every side.

prayer.text: O God, who made St. Arn both bishop and defender of his people in a time of war, grant through his intercession that pastors may guard their flocks with courage and that nations may dwell in peace. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Arnold of Arnoldsweiler
saints.bio:
Arnold of Arnoldsweiler, who died around 800 in Ginnizweiler, today Düren-Arnoldsweiler, is a saint of the Roman Catholic Church, the Orthodox Church, and the True Orthodox Church. He was a musician at the court of Emperor Charles the Great, known as Charlemagne, where his skill with instruments and song served the worship and the gatherings of the imperial household. His feast day is observed on July 18.

Arnold is honored as a patron of musicians, organists, and makers of musical instruments, and he is also invoked for the grace of a good and gentle death. His witness shows that the gifts of art and music, offered to God, can become a path to holiness, and his intercession has long been sought by those who devote their lives to sacred music.

prayer.text: O God, who endowed St. Arnold with the gift of music and the grace of a holy death, grant through his intercession that we may offer you the best of our gifts and, at the hour of our passing, be received into your peace. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arnold of Arnoldsweiler

saints.name: St. Arnold of Soissons
saints.bio:
Arnold was born around 1040 in Brabant, in what is now Belgium. After a career as a soldier, he entered the Benedictine abbey of St. Medard in Soissons, France, and later became its abbot.

He withdrew to a hermitage and eventually founded the abbey of Oudenburg in Flanders, where he served as abbot. He is remembered for his austere life and for miracles attributed to his intercession.

He died around 1087 and was canonized in 1120. He is venerated as the patron saint of brewers, a patronage linked to his abbey's brewing tradition and to the story that he urged people to drink beer rather than unsafe water.

prayer.text: O God, who called Arnold from the soldier's life to the cloister and made him a father to his people, grant through his intercession that brewers may work honestly and bring joy without excess. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arnold of Soissons

saints.name: St. Arnulf of Eynesbury
saints.bio:
Saint Arnulf of Eynesbury is an obscure English saint, apparently a hermit who lived in the eighth or ninth century. He was venerated in Eynesbury, about half a mile from St Neots in Cambridgeshire, during the ninth century, and his memory has been preserved by the local devotion of the faithful across many generations.

Though little is known of his life, Arnulf's witness as a hermit points to the ancient English tradition of solitary holiness, in which men and women withdrew from the world to seek God in silence and prayer. He is honored as one of the hidden saints of early England, whose lives of quiet fidelity helped to sustain the faith of the people among whom they lived and prayed.

prayer.text: O God, who called St. Arnulf to seek you in the solitude of the hermit's life, grant through his intercession that we may find moments of silence amid the noise of the world and draw near to you with undivided hearts. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Arsacius of Tarsus
saints.bio:
Arsacius of Tarsus was the intruding archbishop of Constantinople from 404 to 405, placed in the see after the violent expulsion of St. John Chrysostom by imperial authority. Brother of Nectarius, a predecessor of Chrysostom, Arsacius was already very old when he was installed.

His short and contested episcopate was marked by the deep divisions caused by Chrysostom's exile. Though set up as a rival to a beloved pastor, later tradition, including the Roman Martyrology, remembered Arsacius with leniency, honoring him as a saint and noting that he did not long survive his elevation.

He died in 405, after barely a year in office. His feast day is uncertain, and his cult reflects the complicated aftermath of one of the most painful controversies in early Constantinopolitan church life.

prayer.text: O God, who in Your providence allow even the divisions of Your Church to be gathered back into the communion of saints, grant through the intercession of St. Arsacius that we may work for unity where there has been strife and seek peace where there has been division. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

saints.name: St. Arsatius
saints.bio:
Saint Arsatius, also called Arsacius, is a saint of whose life virtually nothing is known. He is said to have been a bishop of Milan, who lived either around the year 400 or in the sixth century, and possibly a martyr, but there is no evidence for either claim. Because of the traditional connection with Milan, he is supposed to have been a disciple of Saint Ambrose, but there is no evidence of this either.

What survives is only the bare outline of a name and a see, handed down in the calendars of the Church of Milan. He belongs to that large company of early saints whose deeds were lost to history but whose memory the liturgy preserved.

His feast is kept on November 12. The Church honors him as one of the hidden pastors of Milan, linked by tradition to the great Ambrose.

prayer.text: O God, who preserved the memory of St. Arsatius even when the records of his life were lost, grant through his intercession that those who serve You in obscurity may be known to You and rewarded in Your kingdom. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arsatius

saints.name: St. Arsenius the Great
saints.bio:
Arsenius the Deacon, also called Arsenius of Scetis, Arsenius the Roman, or Arsenius the Great, was a Roman imperial tutor who became an anchorite in Egypt, one of the most highly regarded of the Desert Fathers. Born in Rome around 350 and educated in Latin and Greek, he was given the charge of tutoring the sons of the Emperor Theodosius.

Yet the court left him restless. Tradition holds that he prayed and heard a voice saying, "Arsenius, flee from men, and you will be saved." He left Constantinople for the desert of Scetis, where he took up the life of a hermit. His tears were proverbial; he wept for his sins, he said, as one who had been great and was now nothing.

He died around 445. His feast is May 8, and the Church honors him as one who left the courts of emperors for a cell.

prayer.text: O God, who called Arsenius from the courts of emperors to the silence of the desert, grant through his intercession that we may learn to flee from worldly honors and seek You in the stillness of the heart. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Arsenius the Great

saints.name: St. Artemas
saints.bio:
Artemas of Lystra was an early Christian saint named by the Apostle Paul in his Epistle to Titus, where Paul speaks of sending either Artemas or Tychicus to Crete. Honored in both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches, he is believed to have served as Bishop of Lystra in Lycaonia and to have been numbered among the Seventy Disciples whom the Lord Jesus sent out to preach.

His brief mention in Scripture belies a life given to the consolidation and shepherding of churches in the difficult young mission fields of Asia Minor. His feast is kept on October 30, and he is remembered as one of that first generation of pastors who labored to ground the Gospel in the cities where Paul had planted it.

prayer.text: O God, who chose Artemas from among the Seventy and entrusted to him the church of Lystra, grant through his intercession that bishops and pastors may be faithful stewards of the Gospel first preached by the apostles. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

image.altText: Portrait of St. Artemas

saints.name: St. Arthelais
